land.text: Prince Geza's Hungary, which Stephen I turned into a kingdom by his coronation at Esztergom on 25 December 1000

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary row runs 900-999; Cliopatria's 1000 shape adds Transylvania, which the Stephen I page has Stephen taking from Gyula c.1002-1003.

land.text: royal Hungary: 'The territory of present-day Slovakia and northwestern Transdanubia were parts of this polity' (Royal Hungary page); Cliopatria draws these cells in its Kingdom of Spain row from 1540

successors.note: Cliopatria's row ends in 1546. The Kingdom of Hungary page runs the monarchy to 1 February 1946; the Royal Hungary page dates Royal Hungary 1526-1699. The Habsburg Monarchy dossier gains royal Hungary in 1547, although Cliopatria draws the same cells in its 'Kingdom of Spain' row from 1540. Croatia went to Ferdinand at Cetin on 1 January 1527.

land.text: central Hungary taken with Buda on 29 August 1541 and made Budin Province (Ottoman Hungary infobox area about 91,250 km2)

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps this land as the Kingdom of Hungary until 1546 and draws no Hungarian cells in the Ottoman row until later.

land.text: Transylvania and the eastern plain held by John Zapolya, 'after 1571 known as Partium'

successors.note: A rival kingdom from John's coronation on 11 November 1526 (infobox); Cliopatria draws it from 1529 and its dossier names this one as predecessor.

capitals.name: Esztergom
capitals.note: Kingdom of Hungary page: Esztergom 1000-1256; Szekesfehervar stays the crowning and burial site to 1543. The Stephen I page says Stephen made Szekesfehervar 'his new capital'.

capitals.name: Vienna (Bécs)
capitals.note: Matthias Corvinus's court after the Black Army took Vienna; Vienna 1485-1490 on the table

capitals.name: Buda
capitals.note: Buda to 1541 on the table; taken by the Ottomans on 29 August 1541

capitals.name: Pozsony (Pressburg, Bratislava)
capitals.note: Pozsony/Pressburg 1536-1848 on the table; the Royal Hungary page ties the new capital to the 1538 division

correction.text: the kingdom at the coronation without Gyula's Transylvania (valid 1000-1002)

keyframe_review.note: 271,878 km2, 1000-1002. Cliopatria holds Transylvania (191 of its 220 cells) from the coronation, but the page puts Stephen's invasion of Gyula's country at 'around 1002 or in 1003', so the gain event carries Transylvania. The page does not name Ajtony's land (clash 'at the end of the 1020s', Gyorffy at least a decade earlier), so the Banat stays in the shape.

231,939 km2, 1003-1009. Transylvania is inside; 154 Slovak cells are dropped to Poland. The page only says 'parts of Slovakia were under Polish rule between 1002 and 1030' (Steinhubel) and dates the Polish-Hungarian war to about 1014-1018, so the full Slovak loss is partly the researcher's reading (confidence 2).

239,441 km2, 1010-1014. +30 cells on the Danube edge (Iron Gates) taken from the First Bulgarian Empire's shape; page silent (confidence 1). The page has a campaign against Kean, 'Duke of the Bulgarians and Slavs', c.1003 or in the late 1010s.
226,361 km2, 1015-1017. The 52 Danube-edge cells are dropped again; page silent (confidence 1).
265,420 km2, 1018-1027. Slovakia returns (158 cells, all of the difference) at the Peace of Bautzen, January 1018; Steinhubel would keep parts under Polish rule to 1030, so the edge is soft.

265,285 km2, 1028-1039. No cell changes from 1018. Ajtony's defeat and the Csanad bishopric (c.1028 on many historians' dating) are not drawn: the Banat is in the shape since 1000. Conrad II invaded in June 1030 and in summer 1031 ceded the land between the Lajta and Fischa (gain event, too small to show). Stephen died 15 August 1038.
271,855 km2, 1040-1065. +33 cells on the south-eastern edge and -5 to Kievan Rus' in the north-east; the Stephen I page ends in 1038 and is silent on both.
271,466 km2, 1066-1084. unverified: page budget. Kievan Rus' touches the shape by one cell.

271,488 km2, 1085-1093. No change until 1094 in Cliopatria, but the Croatia page dates Ladislaus's conquest of Slavonia to 1091: the 1085 shape holds only to 1090 and the shape of 1094 applies from 1091 (see the new keyframe). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1085..1090 from this entry's own 'valid 1085-1090 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 1094 shape (Slavonia and northern Croatia) from 1091

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1094 shape drawn three years earlier. 'In 1091 Ladislaus crossed the Drava river and conquered the entire province of Slavonia without encountering opposition'; his campaign in Croatia proper was halted near Gvozd.

307,167 km2, 1094-1098. Slavonia and the Pannonian part of Croatia (114 Croatian cells, 133 of them from the Cliopatria Kingdom of Croatia row) after Ladislaus's 1091 conquest. The 21 Bosnian cells are on no page opened: Bosnia is a Hungarian 'Kingdom of Rama' only from 1135 (Banate of Bosnia page).

correction.text: as drawn, valid 1102-1115 and 1133-1138; 1099-1101 take the 1094 shape

keyframe_review.note: 342,621 km2, 1099-1138. Croatia 172, Dalmatia 29 and Bosnia 94 cells. Coloman was crowned at Biograd in 1102 and the Dalmatian towns accepted his suzerainty in 1105 (1000-1301 page; the Croatia page: 'By 1107'), so the shape is three to six years early; for 1099-1101 use the 1094 shape. Croatia stayed a separate kingdom in personal union (Pacta conventa 'viewed as a 14th-century forgery'). The 74 Bosnian cells added in 1099 have no page before 1135. Venice held Dalmatia 1116-1133 (next keyframe).

correction.text: the 1099 shape without the Dalmatian coast, 1116-1132

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Venice 'seized Biograd, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Zadar and several islands' after Coloman's death; Stephen II regained some in 1124 (Venice retook them in 1125) and in 1133 Bela II 'won back the lost cities except Zadar'.
345,440 km2, 1139-1146. unverified: page budget. +11 cells on the north-western edge (Slovakia and the Polish border); page silent.

345,418 km2, 1147-1168. Cliopatria's Byzantine losses start only in 1169; the page: 1163 treaty on Bela's duchy (Croatia and central Dalmatia), Syrmia occupied summer 1164, Dalmatia spring 1165, Sirmium 8 July 1167. This shape holds to 1163.
New keyframe, one year: 'A Byzantine army occupied Syrmia, which became a Byzantine theme' (summer 1164).

New keyframe: Dalmatia occupied spring 1165, 'Dalmatia and Bosnia were soon made Byzantine themes'; the 8 July 1167 treaty 'confirmed Byzantine dominion over central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia'. Cliopatria's 1169 shape has the Dalmatia and Bosnia loss but keeps Syrmia.

323,640 km2, 1169-1176. -85 cells (Dalmatia, Croatia south of the Krka, Bosnia) to the Byzantine Empire, as the page says; Bosnia 'remained under their control until the death of Emperor Manuel I Komnenos in 1180' (Croatia page). Syrmia was Byzantine too but Cliopatria keeps it.

323,618 km2, 1177-1187. Same cells as 1169. Manuel I died 24 September 1180; Bela III restored his suzerainty in Dalmatia by early 1181 and held Syrmia by May 1182, so this shape holds only to 1180. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1177..1180 from this entry's own 'valid 1177-1180 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 1192 shape (Dalmatia, Syrmia and Bosnian edge restored), 1181-1187

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Manuel's death Bela 'reoccupied Croatia, Dalmatia and Sirmia' (1180-1182); Cliopatria shows the recovery only in 1188-1192.

correction.text: the kingdom proper, 1188-1191; Halych is the occupation_start/occupation_end pair

keyframe_review.note: 441,256 km2, 1188-1191. Halych, Pokuttya and northern Moldavia (474 cells, 423 from the Principality of Halych's shape, 251 from Kievan Rus'). The page: Bela 'gave control of Halych to his son Andrew' and styled himself King of Galicia, so the ledger carries it as an occupation, held until 'early 1189 or 1190' ('lost within two years'), not 1191.

334,971 km2, 1192-1201. Infobox area 282,870 km2 for 1200 (Kingdom of Hungary and the 1000-1301 page) against 335.0 k km2 here: ratio 0.84, within the factor of two. Dalmatia and Syrmia restored by Bela III; Venetian attempts on Zadar failed in 1187 and 1193.

353,052 km2, 1202-1205. unverified: page budget. +62 Belgrade-Branicevo cells from the Second Bulgarian Empire's shape; the page is silent. The Fourth Crusade took Zadar in 1202 (the shape keeps it; the ledger marks Zadar contested).
334,712 km2, 1206-1209. unverified: page budget. The 62 cells go back to Bulgaria; page silent.
334,735 km2, 1210-1215. unverified: page budget. No cell change from 1206 beyond 3 Slovak cells.
360,236 km2, 1216-1219. unverified: page budget. +96 Belgrade-Branicevo cells again (94 from the Second Bulgarian Empire); page silent.

361,513 km2, 1220-1235. unverified: page budget. The page has the Golden Bull of 1222, the Cuman submission of 1228 and the Banate of Szoreny in Oltenia in 1231; Cliopatria draws only about 10 of Oltenia's 107 cells, so the march is under-drawn.
334,645 km2, 1236-1240. unverified: page budget. The 97 Belgrade-Branicevo cells go; Bela IV succeeded on 21 September 1235 and was crowned on 14 October 1235.

335,804 km2, 1241-1249. Cliopatria hands 38 north-eastern cells to the Mongol Empire for 1241-1249 and adds 41 Bosnian cells. The pages: the Mongols withdrew in March 1242 and Bela returned in May 1242 to 'a country in ruins'; Coloman 'withdrew from Bosnia after the Tatar invasion of Hungary' in 1241 and Ninoslav retook it (Banate of Bosnia page). The occupation is in the ledger.

349,373 km2, 1250-1259. The Mongol cells (34) return, +17 Belgrade-Branicevo cells five years before the cession of 1255, and Usora and Soli under vassal rulers in the 1250s (Banate of Bosnia page). Rostislav became Ban of Macso in 1254.

New keyframe: 'the Peace of Pressburg, signed on 1 May 1254, under which Ottokar ceded Styria to Bela'; Ottokar won at Kressenbrunn on 12 June 1260 and Bela renounced Styria on 31 March 1261. Cliopatria never draws Styria in the kingdom.
349,418 km2, 1260-1271. Styria is back with Bohemia by the Peace of Vienna of 31 March 1261; the shape never held it.
348,885 km2, 1272-1278. unverified: page budget. 4 cells fewer on the Danube; page silent.
348,839 km2, 1279-1284. unverified: page budget. The Marchfeld battle of 1278 (Ladislaus IV and the Austrians against Bohemia) moved no border.

348,910 km2, 1285-1293. unverified: page budget. The second Mongol invasion (1285-1286) was repulsed; in 1284 Usora and Soli were granted to the deposed Serbian king Dragutin (Banate of Bosnia page), which the shape does not show.
334,038 km2, 1294-1304. unverified: page budget. -64 north-eastern cells to Galicia-Volhynia's shape; page silent.

correction.text: valid 1305-1313: the 1305 shape without Croatia and Slavonia

keyframe_review.note: 291,666 km2, 1305-1313. Cliopatria drops 216 Slovak cells to the Kingdom of Bohemia and adds 52 north-eastern cells from Galicia-Volhynia. The page puts Slovakia in the hands of Matthew III Csak ('fourteen counties') and says Paul Subic and the Babonic family 'achieved de facto independence' in Croatia; 'most territories remained out of royal control' until the 1310s. Croatia is removed here; Slovakia is already out.

349,913 km2, 1314-1325. Cliopatria returns Slovakia (241 cells) in 1314, but Csak 'preserved his autonomy up until his death in 1321' and the Babonic and Subic families 'were only subjugated in 1323'. This shape holds with neither land to 1320 (keyframes 1321 and 1323 follow).
New keyframe: Csak is dead, Slovakia is back; Croatia and Slavonia still under the Subic and Babonic.
New keyframe: the Babonic and Subic are subjugated in 1323; the 1314 shape applies in full.
340,929 km2, 1326-1332. -39 Bosnian cells (Usora and Soli) to the Banate of Bosnia, which Stephen II Kotromanic 'fully annexed in 1324'; two years late.
333,917 km2, 1333-1343. unverified: page budget. -26 south-western cells to the Banate of Bosnia; the page dates Stephen II's gains to 1322-1326 and names no 1333 event.
333,894 km2, 1344-1351. unverified: page budget. Cell-for-cell the same as 1333. The Voivodeship of Maramures is set up in 1343 within the kingdom (to 1402).
334,006 km2, 1352-1362. unverified: page budget. Louis I's Naples campaigns (1347-1351) left no land; see the occupation events.

344,139 km2, 1363-1374. +39 cells: Dalmatia (17 cells from Venice) by the Treaty of Zadar of 18 February 1358, five years early, and 21 eastern cells from the Golden Horde's shape. Louis invaded Bosnia in spring 1363. The Moldavian march (Dragos 1359-60, Bogdan's independence in the early 1360s) is only partly on the page.

338,333 km2, 1375-1384. -27 cells (Bosnia and the Dalmatian hinterland): Tvrtko regained Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum and Usora in March 1367, eight years earlier. The personal union with Poland (Louis crowned at Krakow 17 November 1370; Cliopatria relation 1375-1384) is not territory.
338,723 km2, 1385-1394. unverified: page budget. Louis died in 1382; Charles of Durazzo was murdered in February 1386; Mary was captured in July 1386.
338,793 km2, 1395-1401. unverified: page budget. The Ottoman frontier reached southern Hungary in 1390; Nicopolis 1396 changed no border.
338,699 km2, 1402-1414. unverified: page budget. The Voivodeship of Maramures ends in 1402 (page).

331,691 km2, 1415-1421. -22 Dalmatian coast cells to Venice. Ladislaus of Naples 'sold his rights in Dalmatia to Venice for 100,000 ducats' in 1409 and the republic took the towns 'one by one' in the next decade; 1415 is Cliopatria's year.

331,969 km2, 1422-1439. Three cells at about 51.7N 13.4E (Lower Lusatia) appear with the union with Bohemia and are on no page opened; the union is not territory. Sigismund 'mortgaged 13 Saxon towns in the Szepesseg to Poland in 1412', a pledge the shape does not show.

correction.text: the 1459 shape: Hungary without the Dalmatian coast, 1440-1449

keyframe_review.note: 338,650 km2, 1440-1449. Cliopatria restores 22 Dalmatian cells in 1440 (union with Poland, Wladyslaw 1440-1444) and drops the Lusatian artefact. No page records a Hungarian recovery of the coast after Venice took it in the decade after 1409.

New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1450-1458. The page: the Diet of 1445 acknowledged Ladislaus V, Hunyadi was sole regent from 1446, the Ottomans withdrew from Belgrade on 22 July 1456, Ladislaus V died before the end of 1457.
332,525 km2, 1459-1462. Matthias was proclaimed king on 24 January 1458; Smederevo, and with it Serbia, fell to the Ottomans on 29 June 1459.

correction.text: the 1468 shape, valid from 1463: with the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik

keyframe_review.note: 331,682 km2, 1463-1467. No cell change from 1459, but after 19 July 1463 Matthias 'conquered Jajce and other forts in its northern parts', organised as the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik; Cliopatria draws them only in 1468.
334,526 km2, 1468-1474. +10 Bosnian cells (Jajce and Srebrenik), correct from 1463.

409,969 km2, 1475-1481. +312 cells: Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia. The page: invasion in 1468, Matthias elected king of Bohemia in Olomouc on 3 May 1469 (never crowned), Peace of Olomouc ratified 21 July 1478 leaving Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia to him; the Kingdom of Hungary (1301-1526) page has the peace in 1478 in the text and 2 April 1479 in the infobox.
413,167 km2, 1482-1486. +11 Machva cells (Sabac, captured 15 February 1476, six years early). Matthias 'occupied Lower Austria between 1482 and 1487': hatched in the ledger.

correction.text: the 1482 shape (with Moravia, Silesia and the Machva cells) without Austria, 1487-1491; Lower Austria and Styria as occupation

keyframe_review.note: 466,309 km2, 1487-1491. Lower Austria, Styria and 205 Austrian cells (466 k km2): Cliopatria draws Matthias's conquests as direct land. The pages: the Black Army took Vienna in 1485 and Wiener Neustadt in 1487, Matthias took the title Duke of Austria in 1487, and 'The treaty arranged for the return of Matthias' conquests' (1491); the ledger carries them as occupation.

337,524 km2, 1492-1520. Peace of Pressburg 1491 returned the conquests: Austria to the Habsburgs and, by the same clause, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia (-523 cells). The personal union with Bohemia (1492-1518, Vladislaus II) is not territory.
333,999 km2, 1521-1525. -11 Machva cells; 'In 1521 Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent recognized Hungary's weakness and seized Belgrade'.
324,832 km2, 1526-1528. -34 southern cells (Syrmia and southern Baranya) in the year of Mohacs, 29 August 1526; the pages name no land (confidence 1).

218,990 km2, 1529-1533. -405 cells: the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom's 219 (Transylvania and the Partium; John swore fealty to the sultan on 19 August 1529), Croatia 114 (the Croatian parliament elected Ferdinand at Cetin on 1 January 1527; Cliopatria files Croatia under its Kingdom of Spain row) and 66 southern cells to the Ottomans. The east stays contested with John until the Treaty of Nagyvarad in 1538 (ledger).
241,461 km2, 1534-1539. +85 southern Transdanubian cells from the Ottoman Empire's shape; page silent (confidence 1).

correction.text: 1541-1546: royal Hungary, Slovakia and northwestern Transdanubia; the 1540 shape itself is the Ottoman part

keyframe_review.note: 121,534 km2, 1540-1546. 121.5 k km2 shape that holds none of Slovakia (7 of 195 cells) and none of northwestern Transdanubia: it matches the 'south central and central areas' that fell to the Ottomans (Ottoman Hungary infobox area about 91,250 km2, ratio 1.33, within the factor of two), not the kingdom, which was 'the north-western rim' left to the Habsburgs. Cliopatria draws that rim in its Kingdom of Spain row from 1540. Buda fell on 29 August 1541, so 1540 should still use the 1534 shape and the 1540 shape belongs to Ottoman Hungary from 1541.

region.text: the kingdom Stephen I was crowned to rule (Cliopatria's 1000 shape without Transylvania, which was Gyula's until c.1002/3)

ledger.note: 1000: Stephen I is crowned first king of Hungary at Esztergom on Christmas Day. Infobox: 'Coronation of Stephen I on 25 December 1000, at Esztergom'; the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page: 'on either December 25, 1000, or January 1, 1001'.

region.text: Gyula's country, Transylvania: Stephen 'seized his uncle Gyula and family after invading Transylvania'

ledger.note: c.1002-1003: Stephen I invades Transylvania and seizes his uncle Gyula. The page dates it 'around 1002 or in 1003'; Cliopatria's 1000 shape already contains Transylvania.

region.text: Steinhubel: 'parts of Slovakia were under Polish rule between 1002 and 1030'

ledger.note: c.1003: Slovakia passes to Poland under Boleslaw I (as Cliopatria draws it). The page says 'parts of Slovakia' and gives no 1003-1018 Nitra period; Cliopatria's 1003 shape drops 154 Slovak cells to Poland (156 cells of the Polish row in 1018).

region.text: the 30 cells added at the south-eastern edge in 1010 (lat 43.9-45.2, lon 21.3-23.4)

ledger.note: 1010: Cliopatria adds a strip of the Iron Gates and Banat edge on the Danube (30 cells) from the First Bulgarian Empire. Page silent: the Stephen I page mentions only a campaign against 'Kean, Duke of the Bulgarians and Slavs' (c.1003 or the late 1010s) and Byzantium's war ending in 1018, with no 1010 date or land.

region.text: the Polish-Hungarian war 'ran from about 1014 to 1018'

ledger.note: c.1014: the Polish-Hungarian war over Slovakia begins.

region.text: the 52 cells dropped at the Danube edge in 1015

ledger.note: 1015: Cliopatria withdraws the south-eastern Danube strip (52 cells) it added in 1010. Page silent on 1015; only 5 of the cells fall in the First Bulgarian Empire's own shape, the rest in nobody's.

region.text: the Peace of Bautzen 'reportedly required Boleslaw to hand back Morava valley territories'

ledger.note: January 1018: the Peace of Bautzen returns Slovakia to Hungary. The page does not say Slovakia by name for 1018 and Steinhubel keeps parts under Polish rule to 1030.

region.text: the Peace of Bautzen (January 1018)

ledger.note: January 1018: the Peace of Bautzen ends the Polish-Hungarian war.

region.text: 'in summer 1031 he ceded the lands between the Lajta and Fischa rivers' (after Conrad's June 1030 invasion)

ledger.note: 1031: Conrad II cedes the land between the Lajta and the Fischa to Hungary. The strip is small (about 16 Austrian cells in every Cliopatria shape of the kingdom), so the shape does not change.

region.text: the 33 cells added in 1040 (lat 44.6-49.4, lon 21.3-23.1)

ledger.note: 1040: Cliopatria adds 33 cells on the south-eastern edge (Banat and Oltenia edge). Page silent; Stephen I's page ends in 1038 and gives no later frontier change.

region.text: 'In 1091 Ladislaus crossed the Drava river and conquered the entire province of Slavonia without encountering opposition'

ledger.note: 1091: Ladislaus I crosses the Drava and conquers Slavonia. Cliopatria first draws it in 1094; the page also says his campaign was halted near Gvozd and that Petar Snacic was elected king in 1093 (Knin).

region.text: Croatia proper, where 'Petar Snacic was elected king by Croatian feudal lords in 1093' and Almos was forced back to Hungary in 1095

ledger.note: 1091: Hungary begins the struggle for Croatia proper beyond Gvozd.

region.text: 'Coloman was crowned in Biograd in 1102' (the Kingdom of Hungary page: 'King of Croatia and Dalmatia', a personal union)

ledger.note: 1102: Coloman is crowned king of Croatia and Dalmatia at Biograd. Pacta conventa is 'today viewed as a 14th-century forgery by most modern Croatian historians'; the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page says Croatia was 'never incorporated into Hungary'.

region.text: Croatia proper

ledger.note: 1102: the Biograd coronation ends the Croatian succession struggle.

region.text: 'Zadar, Split, and other Dalmatian towns also accepted Coloman's suzerainty in 1105'

ledger.note: 1105: Zadar, Split and the other Dalmatian towns accept Coloman's suzerainty. Counterpart from the Croatia page: 'By 1107 King Coloman controlled most of former Byzantine coastal cities in Dalmatia'.

region.text: Venice 'defeated Ban Cledin, and seized Biograd, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Zadar and several islands'

ledger.note: 1116: Venice seizes Biograd, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Zadar and the islands after Coloman's death. The page dates the attack to the time after Coloman's death; Stephen II regained some cities in 1124 and Venice retook them in 1125.

region.text: 'In 1133, Bela II won back the lost cities except Zadar'

ledger.note: 1133: Bela II wins back the Dalmatian cities except Zadar.

region.text: the 11 cells added in 1139 (7 inside the Polish row, 4 inside the Holy Roman Empire's)

ledger.note: 1139: Cliopatria adds 11 cells on the north-western edge (the Polish and Moravian border) to the kingdom. Page silent: the answers drawn from the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page list no north-western frontier change before 1202.

region.text: 'A Byzantine army occupied Syrmia, which became a Byzantine theme' after Stephen III's invasion of summer 1164

ledger.note: Summer 1164: a Byzantine army occupies Syrmia, which becomes a Byzantine theme.

region.text: 'A Byzantine army also occupied Dalmatia'; a later treaty confirmed the emperor's suzerainty over Bela's former duchy, 'Dalmatia and Bosnia were soon made Byzantine themes'

ledger.note: Spring 1165: the Byzantines occupy Dalmatia.

region.text: the treaty 'confirmed Byzantine dominion over central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia'

ledger.note: 8 July 1167: the Byzantines destroy the Hungarian army at Sirmium and take central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia by treaty. Cliopatria draws the loss only from 1169.

region.text: 'Early 1181: Zadar accepted Bela's suzerainty'; Manuel I died 24 September 1180, 'within six months' Bela restored his suzerainty in Dalmatia

ledger.note: Early 1181: after Manuel I's death Bela III restores Hungarian suzerainty over Dalmatia, and Zadar accepts it. The page notes there are no detailed contemporary accounts; Cliopatria shows the recovery only in 1188.

region.text: in May 1182 Andronikos accused Bela of ravaging 'the regions of Belgrade and Barancs', implying he already held Syrmia; the page calls the details of the reconquest obscure

ledger.note: By May 1182: Bela III holds Syrmia again.

region.text: Halych, the Cliopatria cells added in 1188 and dropped in 1192 (Galicia, Pokuttya, northern Moldavia)

ledger.note: 1188: Bela III invades Halych, expels Roman Mstislavich and gives the principality to his son Andrew. Page: Vladimir fled to Hungary at the end of 1188 after a boyar revolt; Roman occupied Halych, 'Bela invaded and expelled him', imprisoned Vladimir and 'gave control of Halych to his son Andrew'; Bela styled himself King of Galicia.

region.text: Halych

ledger.note: 1189-1190: Vladimir escapes and, with Casimir II of Poland, expels Andrew from Halych. The page says 'early 1189 or 1190' and that Halych was 'lost within two years'; Cliopatria keeps it to 1191.

region.text: 'the armies of the Fourth Crusade took Zadar in 1202' (the Croatia page: Venetians under Enrico Dandolo and the crusaders 'sacked Zadar')

ledger.note: 1202: the Fourth Crusade takes Zadar from the Hungarian crown. Cliopatria keeps Zadar in the Hungarian shape throughout; the Banate of Bosnia page notes 'Zadar returned to Venice' in 1346, so possession flipped; only Zadar is marked contested.

region.text: the 62 cells added in 1202 (lat 44.3-45.2, lon 19.2-21.8)

ledger.note: 1202: Cliopatria adds the Belgrade-Branicevo country (62 cells) to Hungary. Page silent for 1202-1205; the cells are covered by the Second Bulgarian Empire's own shape in 1201, so that is the counterpart.

region.text: the 63 cells dropped in 1206

ledger.note: 1206: Cliopatria returns the Belgrade-Branicevo country to Bulgaria. Page silent.

region.text: the 96 cells added in 1216 (lat 43.8-45.2, lon 19.2-22.5)

ledger.note: 1216: Cliopatria again adds the Belgrade-Branicevo country (96 cells). Page silent; the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page mentions only Andrew II's undated attempts on Halych.

region.text: Cumania east of the Carpathians (the region is the researcher's reading): 'In 1227, Bela met the Cuman chieftain Boricius, who converted and acknowledged his suzerainty'

ledger.note: 1227: the Cuman chieftain Boricius acknowledges Bela's suzerainty; Bela takes the title King of Cumania in 1233. The Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page: 'persuaded a group of Cumans to accept Andrew II's suzerainty in 1228'; 'Bela adopted the title King of Cumania in 1233'.

region.text: 'established a new march in Oltenia (known as the Banate of Szoreny) in 1231'

ledger.note: 1231: Bela founds the march of Szoreny (the Banate of Severin) in Oltenia. The page names no previous holder. Cliopatria draws only about 10 of Oltenia's 107 cells in the kingdom from 1220, so the shape under-draws the march.

region.text: 'The Bosnian Crusade, led by Bishop John and Coloman, lasted five years' (1235-1240); in 1234 Andrew II gave the banate to Duke Coloman

ledger.note: 1235: Duke Coloman and Bishop John open the five-year Bosnian Crusade.

region.text: the 97 cells dropped in 1236

ledger.note: 1236: Cliopatria returns the Belgrade-Branicevo country to Bulgaria. Page silent.

region.text: 'Coloman withdrew from Bosnia after the Tatar invasion of Hungary. Ninoslav retook control' (1241)

ledger.note: 1241: Coloman withdraws from Bosnia after the Tatar invasion and Ninoslav retakes it. Cliopatria instead adds 38 Bosnian cells to the Hungarian shape in 1241.

region.text: Cumania east of the Carpathians

ledger.note: 1241: the Mongol conquest ends Bela's suzerainty east of the Carpathians. Page silent on the end of the suzerainty; the Bela IV page says only that after Koten's death in a Pest riot 'the Cumans left Hungary' (1241) and were later persuaded to return.

region.text: 'They first occupied and thoroughly plundered the lands east of the Danube' (Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page) (Croatia, Slavonia, Dalmatia and Bosnia lie west of the Danube and are not in the occupied zone: the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page says the Mongols 'first occupied and thoroughly plundered the territories east of the river Danube'; reviewer eu-15-c)

ledger.note: 11 April 1241: the Mongols annihilate Bela IV's army at Mohi and occupy Hungary east of the Danube. Bela IV page: the Mongols 'broke through the Verecke Pass on 12 March 1241'; Bela fled to Trogir.

region.text: 'Batu Khan withdrew his entire army after Ogodei's death in March 1242' (Croatia, Slavonia, Dalmatia and Bosnia lie west of the Danube and are not in the occupied zone: the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page says the Mongols 'first occupied and thoroughly plundered the territories east of the river Danube'; reviewer eu-15-c)

ledger.note: March 1242: Batu withdraws the Mongol army from Hungary after Ogodei's death. Bela IV page: the siege of Trogir in March 1242 'ended when news of Ogodei's death led the Mongols to withdraw'; Bela returned in May 1242 to 'a country in ruins'. Cliopatria keeps the Mongol cells to 1249.

region.text: 'Hungary did control northern Usora and Soli through vassal rulers' (1253); Bela IV 'conquered and pacified Bosnia' and installed Prijezda I as ban

ledger.note: 1250s: Bela IV pacifies Bosnia and controls northern Usora and Soli through vassal rulers. The page says no evidence that the 1253 campaign 'reached the Bosnian Banate' itself.

region.text: 'the Peace of Pressburg, signed on 1 May 1254, under which Ottokar ceded Styria to Bela'

ledger.note: 1 May 1254: by the Peace of Pressburg Ottokar II cedes Styria to Bela IV. Cliopatria draws no Styria in the Hungarian shape of 1250-1259.

region.text: 'In 1255, he forced Tsar Michael Asen I to cede Belgrade and Barancs (Branicevo)'

ledger.note: 1255: Rostislav, Ban of Macso, forces Tsar Michael Asen I to cede Belgrade and Branicevo. Rostislav was appointed Ban of Macso in 1254 and invaded Bosnia the same year. Cliopatria's 1250 shape already contains part of this land.

region.text: 'the Peace of Vienna, signed on 31 March 1261 ... Bela was forced to renounce Styria in favor of the King of Bohemia'

ledger.note: 31 March 1261: by the Peace of Vienna Bela IV renounces Styria in favour of Ottokar II. Ottokar had defeated Bela at Kressenbrunn on 12 June 1260 (the page's date), so the Hungarian hold ended in 1260 de facto.

region.text: the 64 cells dropped in 1294 (lat 44.6-49.4, lon 21.3-24.6)

ledger.note: 1294: Cliopatria hands 64 north-eastern cells (Carpathian Ruthenia) to Galicia-Volhynia. Page silent: the Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page gives no frontier change on the north-eastern edge in the 1290s. [Reviewer eu-15-c: counterpart slug changed from galicia-volhynia to principality-of-galicia-volhynia, whose dossier lists the 'Galicia-Volhynia' Cliopatria row in cliopatria_names.]

14 January 1301: Andrew III dies and the Arpad dynasty ends; the crown passes to the Angevins after the 1301-1308 interregnum. 'Andrew III died on January 14, 1301'; the infobox lists the interregnum as 1301-1308 and says a papal legate 'persuaded all the lords to accept Charles of Anjou's rule in 1310, but most territories remained out of royal control'.

region.text: 'Matthew III Csak ruled over fourteen counties in the lands now forming Slovakia'

ledger.note: 1305: Slovakia slips from royal control into the domain of Matthew Csak. The page does not date the loss; Cliopatria gives the cells to the Kingdom of Bohemia from 1305 (216 cells), which the page does not support. Csak 'preserved his autonomy up until his death in 1321'.

region.text: Paul Subic and the Babonic family 'achieved de facto independence'; Ugrin Csak 'controlled large territories between the rivers Szava and Drava'

ledger.counterpart: Paul Subic and the Babonic family
ledger.note: c.1305: Paul Subic and the Babonic family make themselves independent in Croatia and Slavonia. Undated on the page (it sits in the 1301-1308 interregnum paragraph). The Croatia page: in 1311 Paul Subic 'triggered a revolt in Zadar' and was 'for all practical purposes an independent ruler'. Cliopatria keeps Croatia in the Hungarian shape.

region.text: the 52 cells added in 1305 (lat 47.9-49.0, lon 22.4-24.6)

ledger.note: 1305: Cliopatria returns 52 north-eastern cells (Carpathian Ruthenia) to Hungary from Galicia-Volhynia. Page silent. [Reviewer eu-15-c: counterpart slug changed from galicia-volhynia to principality-of-galicia-volhynia, whose dossier lists the 'Galicia-Volhynia' Cliopatria row in cliopatria_names.]

region.text: Csak 'preserved his autonomy up until his death in 1321'

ledger.note: 1321: Matthew Csak dies and his Slovak domain returns to the crown. The page gives the death and the end of his autonomy, not an explicit royal takeover; 1312: Charles 'won his first victory in the battle of Rozgony'. Cliopatria returns the cells in 1314.

region.text: 'The Babonic and Subic families were only subjugated in 1323'

ledger.counterpart: Paul Subic and the Babonic family
ledger.note: 1323: Charles I subjugates the Babonic and Subic families and recovers Croatia and Slavonia. The Croatia page adds: Battle of Bliska, 1322, where a coalition defeated Mladen II.

region.text: Stephen 'acquired Usora and Soli, which he fully annexed in 1324'

ledger.note: 1324: Stephen II Kotromanic annexes Usora and Soli from the Hungarian crown. Cliopatria drops the 39 Bosnian cells in its 1326 shape. The page: in 1284 'Usora and Soli, which the Hungarian crown had annexed, were granted to the deposed Serbian king Dragutin'.

region.text: the 26 cells dropped in 1333 (lat 43.1-44.4, lon 16.6-17.9)

ledger.note: 1333: Cliopatria hands 26 south-western cells (Dalmatian hinterland) to the Banate of Bosnia. The Banate of Bosnia page dates Stephen II's gains to 1322-1326 (Usora and Soli 1324; Hum, taken from Serbia, by 1326) and names no 1333 event.

region.text: 'He entered the Kingdom of Naples on 24 December' 1347

ledger.note: 24 December 1347: Louis I enters the Kingdom of Naples near L'Aquila. 'He departed from Visegrad on 11 November'; the Black Death forced him out in May 1348, he returned in April 1350 and 'withdrew all his troops from the Kingdom of Naples in 1351'.

region.text: 'He withdrew all his troops from the Kingdom of Naples in 1351'

ledger.note: 1351: Louis I withdraws all his troops from the Kingdom of Naples.

region.text: 'the Republic of Venice renounced all Dalmatian towns and islands between the Gulf of Kvarner and Durazzo in favor of Louis'

ledger.note: 18 February 1358: by the Treaty of Zadar Venice gives up all Dalmatia between the Gulf of Kvarner and Durazzo to Louis I. The Croatia page: 'Venice was forced to sign the Treaty of Zadar on 18 February 1358'. Ragusa 'also accepted Louis's suzerainty' (undated). Cliopatria first draws the gain in 1363.

region.text: Zadar, renounced by Venice in the Treaty of Zadar

ledger.note: 18 February 1358: the Treaty of Zadar ends the contest for Zadar.

region.text: 'Louis invaded Bosnia from two directions in the spring of 1363'

ledger.note: Spring 1363: Louis I invades Bosnia from two directions. Louis page: 'The army under Louis's personal command besieged Sokolac in July, but could not capture it'. Banate of Bosnia page: Vlatko Vukoslavic surrendered Kljuc to Louis, Srebrenik held out ('Tvrtko's first victory against the Hungarian king').

region.text: the cells added in 1363 outside Dalmatia and Bosnia (lat 44-47, lon 21-26.4)

ledger.note: 1363: Cliopatria adds 21 eastern cells (the Moldavian march) taken from the Golden Horde. Page partly silent: Louis I page says a 1360 charter shows Dragos 'restored Louis's suzerainty in Moldavia' (settlement 1359) and that Bogdan then 'expelled the descendants of Louis's vassal, Dragos', so Moldavia was lost again in the early 1360s.

region.text: 'Louis seized Vidin and imprisoned Ivan Stratsimir in May or June ... Within three months, his troops occupied Ivan Stratsimir's realm', which became a border banate under Hungarian lords

ledger.note: May-June 1365: Louis I seizes Vidin and imprisons Tsar Ivan Stratsimir; his troops occupy the realm within three months.

region.text: 'Tvrtko returned and regained Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum, and Usora'

ledger.note: March 1367: Tvrtko I returns and regains Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum and Usora.

region.text: the 27 cells dropped in the 1375 shape (lat 42.8-49.3, lon 14.4-22.3), mostly Bosnia and the Dalmatian hinterland

ledger.note: March 1367: Tvrtko I recovers the Bosnian lands Louis had taken. Banate of Bosnia page: 'In March 1367 Tvrtko returned and regained Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum, and Usora'; Cliopatria draws the loss only in 1375.

region.text: Vidin and Ivan Stratsimir's realm

ledger.note: c.1369: Hungarian control of Vidin ends. Page silent: the Louis I page gives no end to the occupation; the year is a bridging judgment. The Despotate of Vidin runs to 1401 in Cliopatria, whose Vidin shape never carries Hungarian cells.

1387: Sigismund of Luxembourg becomes king, co-ruling from 1387 and alone from 1395. Kingdom of Hungary page: 'Co-ruler from 1387 and sole ruler after 1395'; the 1301-1526 page does not clearly date his accession.

region.text: 'Ladislaus sold his rights in Dalmatia to Venice for 100,000 ducats' (1409)

ledger.note: 1409: Ladislaus of Naples sells his rights in Dalmatia to Venice. Kingdom of Hungary (1301-1526) page: 'In the following decade, the republic forced the settlements on the Dalmatian coasts one by one to accept her suzerainty'.

region.text: the 22 Dalmatian coast cells dropped in 1415

ledger.note: 1415: Venice holds the Dalmatian coast, which Cliopatria removes from the Hungarian shape. The pages give no exact year (the sale was in 1409 and Venice absorbed the towns 'one by one' in the next decade); 1415 is Cliopatria's year. Cliopatria's 1440 shape wrongly puts the coast back.

region.text: the Dalmatian coast

ledger.note: c.1415: the contest for the Dalmatian coast ends in Venetian hands. Bridging year, see the loss event.

Late 1437: Sigismund dies and the Estates elect Albert of Habsburg king. 'Sigismund died in late 1437, and the Estates elected Albert V'; Albert died in 1439 on a campaign against the Ottomans; Wladyslaw was killed at Varna in 1444 and the Diet of 1445 acknowledged Ladislaus V.

24 January 1458: the Estates proclaim Matthias Hunyadi king. 'unanimously proclaimed the 14-year-old Matthias king on 24 January 1458'. Hunyadi's regency (elected sole regent by the Diet of 1446) and the relief of Belgrade (4-22 July 1456) came first.

region.text: 'conquered Jajce and other forts in its northern parts'; 'The conquered areas became the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik' (circles around Jajce and Srebrenik)

ledger.note: After 19 July 1463: Matthias conquers Jajce and northern Bosnia, organised as the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik. Mehmed II had invaded Bosnia in June 1463 and killed King Stephen Tomasevic within a month. Cliopatria first draws the gain in 1468.

region.text: 'In 1468, he invaded Moravia and Silesia' (Lusatia, not in the gazetteer, accepted his rule too)

ledger.note: 31 March 1468: Matthias declares war on George of Podebrady and invades Moravia and Silesia. 3 May 1469: 'The Czech Catholic Estates elected Matthias King of Bohemia in Olomouc ... but he was never crowned'; 'Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia accepted his rule, while Bohemia proper stayed loyal' to George.

region.text: 'the Prince of Moldavia swore fealty to Matthias on 15 August 1475' (Stephen the Great, after the victory at Vaslui on 10 January 1475)

ledger.note: 15 August 1475: the Prince of Moldavia swears fealty to Matthias.

region.text: 'captured Sabac, an important fort on the river Szava, on 15 February 1476'

ledger.note: 15 February 1476: Matthias captures Sabac on the Sava from the Ottomans. Cliopatria draws the 11 Machva cells in 1482.

region.text: 'Matthias invaded Lower Austria and blockaded Vienna' (1477)

ledger.note: 1477: Matthias invades Lower Austria and blockades Vienna.

region.text: the peace 'signed on 1 December 1477'

ledger.note: 1 December 1477: peace with Frederick III, who promises to confirm Matthias as ruler of Bohemia.

region.text: 'They solemnly ratified the peace treaty at their meeting in Olomouc on 21 July 1478': Bohemia proper to Vladislaus, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia to Matthias

ledger.note: 21 July 1478: the Peace of Olomouc leaves Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia to Matthias and Bohemia proper to Vladislaus Jagiellon. The Kingdom of Hungary (1301-1526) page has 'Peace of Olomouc of 1478' in the text and 2 April 1479 in the infobox; Cliopatria draws the gain from 1475.

region.text: Moravia and Silesia

ledger.note: 21 July 1478: the Peace of Olomouc ends the Bohemian war.

region.text: Matthias 'occupied Lower Austria between 1482 and 1487'

ledger.note: 1482: Matthias begins to occupy Lower Austria; the Black Army takes Vienna in 1485. Kingdom of Hungary (1301-1526) page infobox: Vienna, 29 January - 1 June 1485; the war page infobox: 'Black Army captures Vienna'; 'Wiener Neustadt ... captured in 1487'.
1485: Matthias moves his court to Vienna. Capital table: Vienna (Becs) 1485-1490, Buda 1408-1485 and from 1490.

region.text: 'Styria and Lower Austria (including Vienna)' (Kingdom of Hungary (1301-1526) page); 'he adopted the title Duke of Austria in 1487'

ledger.note: 1487: Matthias takes Wiener Neustadt and the title Duke of Austria, and holds Styria. The pages do not date the Styrian conquest; 1487 is Cliopatria's year for the Austrian cells.

region.text: Frederick 'was able to regain the Austrian lands without serious fight' after Matthias died

ledger.note: 1490: after Matthias's death on 6 April, Frederick III regains the Austrian lands without a serious fight. 'died from a stroke on 6 April 1490'; the August date for Maximilian entering Vienna is not on the page.

region.text: Styria

ledger.note: 1490: Styria returns to the Habsburgs with the rest of Matthias's Austrian conquests.
1490: the court returns from Vienna to Buda.

region.text: Moldavia

ledger.note: 1490: Matthias dies and Moldavia's fealty lapses. Page silent on the end of the 1475 fealty; the date is a bridging judgment at Matthias's death.
1490: Matthias dies and Vladislaus II of Bohemia succeeds as king of Hungary. '1490: Matthias died in 1490, and Vladislaus II acceded.'

region.text: 'The treaty arranged for the return of Matthias' conquests'

ledger.note: 1491: the Peace of Pressburg returns Matthias's conquests: Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia go back to Bohemia, Austria to the Habsburgs. The page names no land for the clause; Maximilian also became Vladislaus's heir if he left no heir. Hungary and Bohemia then shared a king (personal union 1492-1518 in Cliopatria).

region.text: 'In 1521 Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent recognized Hungary's weakness and seized Belgrade'

ledger.note: 1521: Suleiman seizes Belgrade. Cliopatria drops 11 Machva cells in 1521 and 34 southern cells in 1526.

29 August 1526: Louis II is killed at Mohacs and the crown passes to rival kings. Infobox battle date 29 August 1526; after Mohacs the nobles 'simultaneously elected two kings'; Zapolya was elected 10 November 1526 and Ferdinand in December 1526 (Kingdom of Hungary page).

region.text: the 34 cells dropped in 1526 (lat 44.6-46.2, lon 18.3-20.0)

ledger.note: 1526: Cliopatria drops 34 southern cells (Syrmia and southern Baranya) after Mohacs. Page silent on the land: the Ottoman Hungary page covers Syrmia only for 1716-1718 and gives Mohacs only as a year.

region.text: 'The Croatian parliament unanimously elected Ferdinand of the House of Habsburg as King of Croatia' at Cetin on 1 January 1527

ledger.note: 1 January 1527: the Croatian parliament at Cetin elects Ferdinand of Habsburg king of Croatia. Cliopatria draws Croatia in its 'Kingdom of Spain' (Habsburg) row from 1529 (104 cells) and loses 114 Croatian cells from the Hungarian shape in 1529; the Habsburg Monarchy row has none.

region.text: the territory John held: Transylvania and the eastern plain (Cliopatria's Eastern Hungarian Kingdom shape of 1529)

ledger.note: By 1528: Ferdinand's army drives John Zapolya out of the country; the two kings contest the realm. 'Ferdinand's army drove John from the country by 1528'; John's coronation is dated 11 November 1526 in the infobox and his oath of fealty to the sultan 19 August 1529.

region.text: the 85 cells added in 1534 (lat 44.6-48.1, lon 16.4-20.0)

ledger.note: 1534: Cliopatria returns 85 southern Transdanubian cells to Hungary from the Ottoman Empire. Page silent: no page opened dates a Hungarian recovery in the 1530s.

region.text: John held Transylvania and the eastern Hungarian plain; Ferdinand 'held Croatia, the western plain, and Upper Hungary'

ledger.note: 24 February 1538: the Treaty of Nagyvarad divides the kingdom between Ferdinand and John.

region.text: Transylvania and the eastern plain, which 'after 1571 became known as Partium'

ledger.note: 24 February 1538: John Zapolya keeps Transylvania and the eastern plain. 'Temporary territorial division between the rival rulers John I and Ferdinand I occurred only in 1538, under the Treaty of Nagyvarad' (Royal Hungary page); Ferdinand also became John's heir.

1541: with Buda lost, the Habsburg kingdom is governed from Pressburg (Pozsony). Kingdom of Hungary page capital table: 'Pozsony/Pressburg 1536-1848'; the Royal Hungary page ties the new capital Pressburg to the 1538 division.

region.text: 'south central and central areas of the kingdom came under the authority of the Ottoman Empire' (the 121,500 km2 shape Cliopatria draws from 1540 matches the Ottoman Hungary infobox area of about 91,250 km2)

ledger.note: 29 August 1541: the Ottomans take Buda and central Hungary becomes Budin Province. Kingdom of Hungary page: 'Ottoman occupation on 29 August 1541'; Eastern Hungarian Kingdom page: Suleiman 'took most of central Hungary under direct Ottoman rule as Budin Province'.

region.text: royal Hungary: 'The territory of present-day Slovakia and northwestern Transdanubia were parts of this polity' (Royal Hungary page); Cliopatria draws these cells in its Kingdom of Spain row from 1540

ledger.note: 1546: Cliopatria's row ends; royal Hungary passes to the Habsburg Monarchy, central Hungary to the Ottomans, the east to the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom. Page silent on an end in 1546: the Kingdom of Hungary page runs the monarchy to 1 February 1946 and Royal Hungary is dated 1526-1699. 1546 is Cliopatria's last year and the point where the Habsburg Monarchy dossier takes over (its 1547 gain).

wars.name: Stephen I's wars against Gyula, Ajtony and Kean
wars.outcome: Stephen subdues his uncle Gyula and Transylvania; Ajtony is killed by Csanad's army and a bishopric is set up at Csanad; the campaign against Kean is dated c.1003 or the late 1010s.
wars.note: Ajtony's clash is dated 'to the end of the 1020s' by many historians, a decade earlier by Gyorffy; the page names no land for it, so no zone.

wars.name: Polish-Hungarian War (1014-1018)
wars.outcome: The Peace of Bautzen (January 1018) 'reportedly required Boleslaw to hand back Morava valley territories'; Steinhubel keeps parts of Slovakia under Polish rule to 1030.

wars.name: Conrad II's invasion of Hungary

zones.text: the lands between the Lajta and Fischa

wars.outcome: 'Emperor Conrad personally led his armies to Hungary in June 1030', withdrew, and in summer 1031 ceded the lands between the Lajta and Fischa rivers.

wars.name: Conquest of Slavonia and the Croatian succession struggle
wars.outcome: Ladislaus I conquers Slavonia in 1091; Petar Snacic is elected king in 1093 at Knin and Almos is forced back in 1095; Coloman is crowned in Biograd in 1102.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian wars for Dalmatia (1116-1133)

zones.text: Biograd, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Zadar and the islands

wars.outcome: Venice takes the coastal cities after Coloman's death; Stephen II regains some in 1124, Venice retakes them in 1125, and in 1133 Bela II wins back all but Zadar.

wars.name: Byzantine-Hungarian War (1163-1167)

zones.text: Bela's former duchy: central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia

wars.outcome: Manuel I occupies Syrmia (1164) and Dalmatia (1165) and destroys the Hungarian army at Sirmium on 8 July 1167; the peace 'confirmed Byzantine dominion over central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia'.

wars.name: Bela III's recovery of Dalmatia and Syrmia
wars.outcome: After Manuel I's death on 24 September 1180 Bela restores his suzerainty in Dalmatia by early 1181 and holds Syrmia by May 1182; in the first half of 1183 he advances as far as Nis and Serdica.
wars.note: The page calls the details obscure and notes no detailed contemporary accounts.

wars.name: Hungarian occupation of Halych (1188-1190)
wars.outcome: Bela III expels Roman Mstislavich and gives Halych to his son Andrew; Vladimir escapes and, with Casimir II of Poland, expels Andrew in early 1189 or 1190.

wars.name: Fourth Crusade at Zadar
wars.outcome: 'the armies of the Fourth Crusade took Zadar in 1202'; Zadar stayed contested between Venice and the Hungarian crown until the Treaty of Zadar of 1358.

wars.name: Bosnian Crusade
wars.outcome: Duke Coloman and Bishop John campaign for five years (1235-1240); Coloman withdraws in 1241 after the Tatar invasion and Ninoslav retakes control.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Hungary

zones.text: 'the lands east of the Danube' occupied and plundered

wars.outcome: The Mongols break through the Verecke Pass on 12 March 1241, annihilate Bela IV's army at Mohi on 11 April, cross the frozen Danube in early 1242 and withdraw in March 1242 after Ogodei's death.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Hungary (1000-1301) page is the source for the Danube crossing and Batu's withdrawal. Cliopatria keeps Mongol cells in north-eastern Hungary to 1249.

wars.name: Bela IV's war with Ottokar II over Styria
wars.outcome: Peace of Pressburg 1 May 1254: Styria to Bela; Ottokar wins at Kressenbrunn on 12 June 1260; Peace of Vienna 31 March 1261: Bela renounces Styria.

wars.name: Charles I's wars against the oligarchs
belligerents: Paul Subic and the Babonic family

zones.text: Croatia and Slavonia under the Subic and Babonic

wars.outcome: After the Arpad line ended on 14 January 1301 'most territories remained out of royal control'; Charles won at Rozgony in 1312, Csak died in 1321 and the Babonic and Subic were subjugated in 1323.

wars.name: Louis I's Neapolitan campaigns
wars.outcome: Louis enters the kingdom on 24 December 1347, leaves in May 1348 because of the Black Death, returns in April 1350 and withdraws all troops in 1351.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian War of 1356-1358

zones.text: Dalmatia between the Gulf of Kvarner and Durazzo

wars.outcome: Louis invades Venetian lands in summer 1356, besieges Treviso on 27 July and marches to Dalmatia in July 1357; by the Treaty of Zadar (18 February 1358) Venice renounces Dalmatia.

wars.name: Louis I's war in Bosnia

zones.text: Donji Kraji, Usora, Rama and Hum

wars.outcome: Louis invades in spring 1363 and takes Kljuc, but Srebrenik holds; in March 1367 Tvrtko returns and regains Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum and Usora.

wars.name: Louis I's Vidin campaign

zones.text: Vidin and the realm of Ivan Stratsimir

wars.outcome: Louis seizes Vidin and imprisons Ivan Stratsimir in May or June 1365 and his troops occupy the realm within three months.

wars.name: Crusade of Nicopolis
wars.outcome: The crusaders 'were routed in the battle of Nicopolis in 1396'; no territorial change is stated.

wars.name: Venetian takeover of the Dalmatian coast
wars.outcome: Ladislaus of Naples sells his claims to Venice in 1409 and 'the republic forced the settlements on the Dalmatian coasts one by one to accept her suzerainty'.
wars.note: The Hungary (1301-1526) page gives no exact years; the span end 1420 is the Croatia page's 'decade' reading and is not a page date.

wars.name: Crusade of Varna
wars.outcome: 'The Ottomans annihilated the Christian forces at the Battle of Varna in 1444, during which Wladyslaw was killed'; no territorial change is stated.

wars.name: Bohemian-Hungarian War (1468-1478)
wars.outcome: Matthias declares war on George of Podebrady on 31 March 1468, is elected king of Bohemia at Olomouc on 3 May 1469; the Peace of Olomouc ratified on 21 July 1478 gives him Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia and Vladislaus Bohemia proper.

wars.name: Matthias Corvinus's Bosnian campaign
wars.outcome: After Mehmed II's conquest of Bosnia in June 1463 Matthias takes Jajce and the northern forts, organised as the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik.

wars.name: Matthias Corvinus's Ottoman wars
wars.outcome: Matthias captures Sabac on 15 February 1476, helps Moldavia win at the Siret in August 1476 and at Breadfield on 13 October 1479.
wars.note: Moldavia's Prince swore fealty to Matthias on 15 August 1475.

wars.name: Austrian-Hungarian War (1477-1488)
wars.outcome: Hungarian victory: the Black Army takes Vienna in 1485 and Wiener Neustadt in 1487; after Matthias's death on 6 April 1490 Frederick III regains the Austrian lands without a serious fight and the Peace of Pressburg (1491) returns Matthias's conquests.
wars.note: Peace of 1 December 1477 is on the Matthias Corvinus page; the armistice of St. Polten was 6 December 1488.

wars.name: Dozsa Rebellion
wars.outcome: The peasant revolt of 9 April - 15 July 1514 (infobox dates) changed no frontier.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Belgrade and the Battle of Mohacs
wars.outcome: Suleiman seizes Belgrade in 1521 and defeats the Hungarian army at Mohacs on 29 August 1526, where Louis II drowns.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Hungary page gives the battle date and Louis II's death.

wars.name: War of the two kings (Ferdinand and John Zapolya)
wars.outcome: Two kings are elected (Zapolya on 10 November 1526, Ferdinand in December); Ferdinand's army drives John out by 1528; John swears fealty to the sultan on 19 August 1529; the Treaty of Nagyvarad (24 February 1538) divides the kingdom.

wars.name: Ottoman occupation of central Hungary
wars.outcome: Buda is taken by a trick on 29 August 1541 and central Hungary becomes Budin Province; the royal remainder is governed from Pressburg.

certainty.note: Frontiers are approximate throughout: the Carpathian march, the Danube and Sava lines to Bulgaria and Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia (a union and a vassalage rather than a border), the Halych and Mongol episodes.

The Dalmatian coast is a treaty line from the Treaty of Zadar (18 February 1358) to the Venetian takeover after 1409; the Bohemian line follows the Peace of Olomouc (21 July 1478), the Austrian line the Peace of 1 December 1477 and the Peace of Pressburg (1491); the Bosnian and Ottoman march stays soft.
The 24 February 1538 Treaty of Nagyvarad is a dated division but no survey line; the Ottoman-Habsburg front after 1541 is approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: one row, 1000..1546, 56 shapes, all reviewed. The Wikipedia article's kingdom runs to 1946; identity.end 1546 follows Cliopatria's last shape and the Habsburg Monarchy dossier's 1547 gain, and the dissolve event is a map-boundary event at confidence 1 (page silent).

Biggest Cliopatria problems found:
(1) The 1540-1546 shape (121,5 k km2) holds none of Slovakia or north-western Transdanubia: it is the Ottoman-occupied centre (Ottoman Hungary infobox about 91,250 km2), while royal Hungary is drawn under Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Spain' row from 1540 to 1555 (Slovakia 184, Hungary 90, Croatia 101 cells in 1545) and Croatia from 1529. Verdict adjust; the Habsburg Monarchy dossier gains the same land in 1547. The colour agent should decide whether Spain's Habsburg cells in Hungary and Croatia belong to habsburg-monarchy.
(2) Halych 1188-1191 (474 cells) is really a short occupation (1188 to early 1189 or 1190).
(3) Slovakia 1305-1313 is given to Bohemia; the page says Matthew III Csak held it until his death in 1321; Croatia was held by the Subic and Babonic until 1323.
(4) Dalmatia: 1099 is 3-6 years early; the Venetian years 1116-1133 and the Byzantine years 1164-1180 are missing; the 1440-1449 shape wrongly gives the coast back after Venice took it (1409-c.1420).
(5) 1241-1249: Mongol cells held to 1249 (page: withdrew March 1242) and 38+ Bosnian cells added in 1241 (page: Coloman withdrew in 1241).
(6) Moravia, Silesia (1475) and Austria (1487-1491) are drawn as direct land; Austria is better an occupation.
(7) The Belgrade-Branicevo country swings 1202-1205, 1216-1235 and from 1250 with no page found for the first two spans.

Shapes with verdict ok and the note 'unverified: page budget' (or page silent): 1066, 1139, 1202, 1206, 1210, 1216, 1220, 1236, 1272, 1279, 1285, 1294, 1333, 1344, 1352, 1385, 1395, 1402. Events at confidence 1: 1010, 1015, 1040, 1202, 1206, 1216, 1236, 1241 (Cuman end), 1294, 1305 (three), 1333, 1363 (Golden Horde cells), 1369, 1415, 1490 (Moldavia), 1526, 1534, 1546. A gap-filler could open: Emeric and Andrew II (Belgrade-Branicevo, Halych 1214-1219), Banate of Macso, Voivodeship of Maramures, Sigismund (Bosnia, Dalmatia 1409-1420, Bohemia 1419/1436), John Hunyadi, Peace of Pressburg (1491) and the Treaty of Nagyvarad.

Pages that would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Croatia_(1102–1526) (url_not_found); replaced by 'Croatia in union with Hungary', which opened.

Personal unions (not territory): Poland 1370-1382 (Cliopatria 1375-1384), Bohemia 1419-1439 and 1490-1526 (Cliopatria 1422-1439, 1492-1518, 1516-1528), the Polish-Lithuanian union 1440-1444 (Cliopatria 1440-1449); the pages opened give no ledger event for them. Croatia (1102-1527) and Dalmatia are in personal union and the Kingdom of Croatia row ends in 1098: a dossier for Croatia in union with Hungary / Slavonia is needed; so are Kingdom of Syrmia's links (Dragutin, 1284-1325).

The ruler strip is omitted: no 'List of Hungarian monarchs' page was opened.

Not drawn but on the pages: Cumans settled in the central plain (1239-1241), the Voivodeship of Maramures 1343-1402, 13 Saxon towns of the Szepesseg mortgaged to Poland in 1412 (never redeemed in the pages), Ragusa's suzerainty to Louis (1358, undated), Jajce and Srebrenik banates after 1463, Hussite raids from 1428, Golubac (Ottoman 1427), Moldavia's fealty 1475.

Region names the gazetteer lacks: Transdanubia, Lusatia, Szepesseg (Spis), Jajce, Srebrenik, Sabac, Visegrad, Mohacs. Used as plain circles or in text where possible; Transdanubia is used in the Mongol occupation events and the Mongol war zone.
